title: Pixel Art
body:
Goal: turn a list of strings into a picture with a nested loop (a loop inside a loop).

"..G.....G.."   <- row 0: the inner loop walks along it, pixel by pixel
"...G...G..."   <- row 1: the outer loop moves down to the next row
  1. Open starter.py and press Run. Only the top row appears.
  2. TODO 1: add the outer loop for row in grid: so every row is drawn. Remember to indent the inner loop and to move down: y = y - size.
  3. TODO 2: finish count_pixels() with a loop inside a loop.
  4. Design your own picture! Copy INVADER, give it a new name and change the letters. Every row should be the same length.

Done looks like: a green space invader with black eyes, and Green pixels: 46 printed in the Shell.

Extra: draw two pictures side by side, or make draw_grid take an x and y for where the picture starts.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run it and look at the picture. Only the top row shows up, because draw_grid() uses grid[0] and nothing else. Read TODO 1 and TODO 2 in starter.py.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: A nested loop is a loop inside a loop. The outer loop picks one row, and the inner loop walks along that row. In draw_grid(), the lines that draw a row go inside the outer loop, and y has to move down after each row.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Use this shape: for ____ in grid: then, indented below it, for ____ in ____:. In count_pixels(), add 1 to count when pixel == ____. In draw_grid(), finish each row with y = y - ____.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Pixel Art
# The picture is a list of strings: one string per row, one letter per pixel.

import turtle

# K = black, O = orange, Y = yellow, B = blue, S = sky blue,
# G = green, R = vermillion, P = purple, . = empty
INVADER = [
    "..G.....G..",
    "...G...G...",
    "..GGGGGGG..",
    ".GGKGGGKGG.",
    "GGGGGGGGGGG",
    "G.GGGGGGG.G",
    "G.G.....G.G",
    "...GG.GG...",
]


def color_for(pixel):
    """Return the color code for one letter of the picture."""
    if pixel == "K":
        return "#000000"
    elif pixel == "O":
        return "#E69F00"
    elif pixel == "Y":
        return "#F0E442"
    elif pixel == "B":
        return "#0072B2"
    elif pixel == "S":
        return "#56B4E9"
    elif pixel == "G":
        return "#009E73"
    elif pixel == "R":
        return "#D55E00"
    elif pixel == "P":
        return "#CC79A7"
    else:
        return "white"


def count_pixels(grid, letter):
    """Return how many times a letter appears in the whole grid."""
    count = 0
    # TODO 2: a loop inside a loop: for row in grid:  then  for pixel in row:
    # add 1 to count when the pixel is the letter.
    return count


def draw_square(t, x, y, size, color):
    """Draw one filled square with its top-left corner at (x, y)."""
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.setheading(0)
    t.pendown()
    t.color("black", color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for _ in range(4):
        t.forward(size)
        t.right(90)
    t.end_fill()


def draw_grid(t, grid, size):
    """Draw every pixel that is not '.', row by row, from the top."""
    y = len(grid) * size / 2
    # TODO 1: this only draws the FIRST row (grid[0]).
    # Wrap the lines below in an outer loop:  for row in grid:
    # and after each row move down:  y = y - size
    row = grid[0]
    x = -len(row) * size / 2
    for pixel in row:
        if pixel != ".":
            draw_square(t, x, y, size, color_for(pixel))
        x = x + size


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"Green pixels: {count_pixels(INVADER, 'G')}")
    turtle.tracer(0)                       # draw everything at once (fast)
    t = turtle.Turtle()
    t.hideturtle()
    draw_grid(t, INVADER, 30)
    turtle.update()
    turtle.done()
